claims.claim: Volcano erupts, spewing ash over surrounding areas, causing widespread disruption and damage.
claims.evidence: Taal Volcano eruption caused disruption and damage
claims.quote: Taal Volcano in Batangas, Philippines began to erupt on January 12, 2020, when a phreatomagmatic eruption from its main crater spewed ashes over Calabarzon, Metro Manila, and some parts of Central Luzon and Ilocos Region

claims.claim: Taal Volcano in the Philippines began to erupt on January 12, 2020, with a phreatomagmatic eruption from its main crater, as reported by the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology.
claims.evidence: Taal Volcano eruption date and type
claims.quote: Taal Volcano in Batangas, Philippines began to erupt on January 12, 2020, when a phreatomagmatic eruption from its main crater spewed ashes over Calabarzon, Metro Manila, and some parts of Central Luzon and Ilocos Region

claims.claim: The eruption produced loud rumbling sounds and ash that affected nearby regions, including Calabarzon, Metro Manila, and parts of Central Luzon and Ilocos Region, resulting in the suspension of school classes and work schedules.
claims.quote: Loud rumbling sounds were also felt and heard from the volcano island. By 2:30 pm, PHIVOLCS raised the alert status to Alert Level 2, although PHIVOLCS through its Taal Volcano Observatory had advised residents of Volcano Island to evacuate at around 1 pm. Stronger explosions began around 3 pm that spewed an ash column

claims.claim: The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology issued an Alert Level 4, indicating a hazardous explosive eruption was possible within hours to days, prompting evacuations and precautions in the surrounding areas.
claims.quote: The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) subsequently issued an Alert Level 4, indicating 'that a hazardous explosive eruption is possible within hours to days.'

claims.claim: Volcanic activity continued into 2021 and 2022, with smaller eruptions occurring in July 2021 and March 2022, demonstrating the ongoing volatility of the volcano.
claims.quote: Volcanic activity continued into 2021, when smaller eruptions occurred in July 2021. On March 26, 2022, a short-lived phreatomagmatic eruption was recorded by PHIVOLCS raising the status from Alert level 2 to Alert level 3.

claims.claim: The eruptions caused significant disruptions to daily life, including the suspension of school classes and flights, as well as environmental damage, such as the temporary drying up of Taal Main Crater Lake and the destruction of Vulcan Point.
claims.evidence: Disruptions and environmental damage caused by eruptions
claims.quote: resulting in the suspension of school classes, work schedules, and flights in the area, as well as temporarily drying up Taal Main Crater Lake and destroying Vulcan Point, an Island surrounded by the lake.
